reason: Contribution is agent-tuning: adding a prefix/suffix to successful vs unsuccessful trajectories when fine-tuning; no runtime control structure is studied.
Introduces a physical agentic loop with a Watchdog execution-monitoring layer and a bounded policy that finalizes, retries or escalates, guaranteeing finite termination.
Compares a single-agent baseline against three multi-agent reasoning topologies (peer review, triage-ranking, triage-forms) in an active-learning discovery loop.
Proposes a multi-agent architecture with eight retrieval agents plus a dedicated verification agent that judges the code its counterparts generate.
Self-described survey of LLM agent methodology, applications and challenges with a methodology-centered taxonomy; secondary study, snowballing seed.
Multi-agent framework whose agents extract, synthesize and self-evaluate, with ablation studies validating the effectiveness and synergy of each agent.
Retrospex rescores the LLM agent's action likelihood with an offline RL critic and uses dynamic action rescoring, changing action selection at each interaction step.
Fine-tunes LLMs and an LVLM with a policy-gradient algorithm and tests reasoning on eight datasets; no iterative control at inference.
Self-described tutorial surveying LLM limitations, RAG/PAL/ReAct/LangChain, fine-tuning strategies and transformer architectures; no method contribution.
Alignment Fine-Tuning with a constraint alignment loss over ranked chain-of-thought responses; the object is training loss, not runtime control.
Replaces single-pass autoregressive generation with iterative resampling of individual variables via LLM conditionals; the iteration policy is the contribution.
Essay and literature review of four categories of LLM deception (strategic, imitation, sycophancy, unfaithful reasoning) and their governance implications.
Rubric-based reward models are used to steer agents at interaction time on multi-step reasoning and tool-use tasks without retraining, a test-time control component.
Self-described critical review giving a comprehensive overview of causal reasoning benchmarks for LLMs and criteria they should satisfy.
HELPER retrieves from an external memory of language-program pairs on each dialogue turn or correction and expands that memory during deployment.
Uses LLM agents as off-the-shelf simulation tools in Trust Games to compare agent trust with human trust behavior; no claim about the agents' control structure.
Self-described comprehensive survey of the agent skills landscape organized along four axes, identifying seven open challenges; secondary study.
AgentGen synthesizes environments and planning tasks for instruction tuning; the contribution is agent training data, not a runtime loop.
Agent-Driver replaces the perception-prediction-planning pipeline with a tool library, cognitive memory and a reasoning engine doing chain-of-thought and self-reflection.
Systematic review of RL across the LLM lifecycle, collating datasets, benchmarks and open-source training frameworks; secondary study, snowballing seed.
CROP is automatic prompt optimization that regularizes response length via textual feedback; prompt engineering, not runtime control return.
BALAR is a task-agnostic outer-loop algorithm maintaining a belief state, selecting the next clarifying question by expected mutual information and expanding its state.
Adds a length-difference positional encoding and fine-tunes so responses terminate at a target token length; no iterative control at inference.
Controlled study of four agentic issue-resolution frameworks finding framework architecture is the primary driver of energy and that energy is spent on unproductive reasoning loops.
Comprehensive survey of LLM-brained GUI agents covering frameworks, data, action models and benchmarks; secondary study, snowballing seed.
Husky iterates between generating the next action over a unified action space and executing it while updating the solution state.
Learning to Plan iteratively updates a task plan with new solutions and behavioral instructions derived by prompting LLMs on error feedback.
WKVQuant is a post-training quantization framework for weights and the KV cache; about deployment memory cost, not any agent control structure.
Binary classification of tutor praise responses plus LLM-facilitated named entity recognition for feedback; single-pass classification, no loop.
Maintains an external VAD state across a 25-turn dialogue, injects it back into generation, and compares stateless, first-order and second-order dynamics.
The three stated contributions are a tool environment, data curation and a cascaded SFT-then-RL training recipe for STAgent; the object is the trained policy.
Natural language dialogue between agents enabling collaborative analysis refinement is named the system's key feature, not an off-the-shelf loop.
Benchmarks five LLMs on 166 ICPC problems for correctness, resource use and calibration; measures one-shot solving, not any loop property.
SOPBench measures whether language agents' tool calls follow SOPs and constraints across 24k trajectories, including how easily they are jailbroken into ignoring them.
Compares base, custom and fine-tuned GPT models on classification accuracy against human coding of 88 and 238 ESG papers; single-pass classification.
Lang-PINN's Feedback Agent executes generated PINN code and diagnoses errors for iterative refinement, a designed execute-diagnose-repair cycle.
Retrieve-then-generate RAG over Quranic surah descriptions, scoring 13 models on context relevance and faithfulness; one pass, no re-query on a failed check.
Trial-and-demonstration framework trains a language model from scratch with teacher demonstrations and a reward; a training loop, not inference-time control.
Attributes agent failures to long-horizon context management and hallucination about task state, then adds explicit belief state representations to mitigate them.
Zero-shot chain-of-thought classifier scores class membership relations from entity and class descriptions; single-pass classification with no feedback.
Tests proprietary and fine-tuned open-source LLMs as one-shot evaluators of palliative care conversation scripts for understanding and empathy.
Causal Agent is built from tool, memory and reasoning modules, where the reasoning module performs multiple iterations with the tools and memory holds causal graphs.
Self-generated cross-modal alignment data (DeSTA-AQA5M) for training an audio language model; the contribution is a data construction pipeline for training.
Three-step learning algorithm that generates refinements from language feedback and then finetunes GPT-3 on the chosen refinement; refinement is distilled into weights.
Explains the behavior of robot and deep-network agents from observed states and actions; the agent being explained is not a language-model agent with a control loop.
